messages:
sarah_ops: :rotating_light: I'm seeing a sudden spike in auth failures for API keys since ~08:12 UTC. Multiple customers reporting 401s. Logs show `auth-service` returning 500s then 401s. Noted from PROD metrics dashboard.
matt_reliability: copying — do we know if anything deployed around that time?
sarah_ops: deploy-bot shows a config rollout to auth-config at 08:10 (env: prod).
deploy-bot: deploy finished: service=auth-config, version=v2026.03.15-814, target=prod, by=kai_auth.
jenna_support: three high-priority tickets opened by enterprise customers complaining: "API keys stopped working" — they included curl traces showing `401 Unauthorized`.
luis_oncall: I'm taking lead. @kai_auth can you confirm what changed in that rollout?
kai_auth: rolled a key-management change — rotating signed key for oauth-introspect and updated the jwks endpoint cache TTL. It completed at 08:10. I ran unit tests and staging smoke. Didn't see prod errors in canary.
matt_reliability: logs from auth-service show a cascade: first internal 500s against kms-proxy, then token introspection start returning 401 for previously-valid tokens. snippet: ```
[08:11:02] auth-service ERROR introspect: unexpected response from kms-proxy: 500
[08:11:07] auth-service WARN token: failed-verify key_id="rot-2026-03-15" err="invalid_signature"
[08:11:12] gateway INFO upstream responded 401 user=api-key-xxxx
```
sarah_ops: paging history: pagerbot alerted at 08:12. We got initial customer reports ~08:13.
pagerbot: page: luis_oncall, matt_reliability — 3 minutes since threshold breached.
luis_oncall: immediate mitigation: can we toggle fallback to previous JWKS? There's a flag in auth-config: `auth.introspection.enable_jwks_fallback`.
kai_auth: I can flip it, but need to confirm keys are still present in KMS. Running `gcloud kms keys versions list` against key ring.
jenna_support: meanwhile I asked customers for request IDs and timestamps to correlate. Some provided x-request-id: `req_8a7c9c`.
matt_reliability: quick check: curl to jwks endpoint returns the rotated key only; old key removed. If services expected both during overlap we broke backward compatibility. `curl -s https://auth.prod/jwks | jq '.keys[].kid'` => ["rot-2026-03-15"] only.
sarah_ops: that explains invalid_signature. Many token validators still using cached kid. We should have published both keys for 24h overlap.
kai_auth: root cause: my rollout removed legacy key earlier than planned — a config typo in the rollout manifest (`remove_legacy_key: true` set) instead of `remove_legacy_key: scheduled`. I'm deploying rollback now.
deploy-bot: executing: `kubectl apply -f auth-config-rollback.yaml --namespace=prod`
matt_reliability: while rollback runs, enable token validation fallback so introspection will accept either JWK by kid mapping from old verification cache. Add temporary permissive check: `allow_missing_kid=true` to reduce immediate 401s.
luis_oncall: perf/latency note: enabling permissive check increases CPU on auth-service ~10%, but better than ongoing 401s. I'm okay with the trade for 30m.
kai_auth: rollback applied, running `kubectl rollout status deployment/auth-config -n prod`. Seeing config reconcile at 08:22.
sarah_ops: customers starting to report partial recovery ~08:25. Ticket updates: "most endpoints working again, some tokens still 401".
matt_reliability: auth-service logs after rollback: ```
[08:22:10] auth-service INFO jwks: published legacy key kid="legacy-2025-11" -> available
[08:22:35] gateway INFO upstream responded 200 user=api-key-xxxx
```
jenna_support: updating affected customers: rollback in progress, asking them to retry after 5 minutes.
luis_oncall: mitigation checklist: 1) rollback config (done) 2) enable permissive validation (done) 3) scale auth-service +2 pods to absorb extra CPU (scaling now) 4) monitor for consumer 401s over next 30m.
matt_reliability: scaling complete: `kubectl scale deployment/auth-service --replicas=8 -n prod` executed.
kai_auth: follow-up: I mistakenly removed the `staged_key_retention` field in the manifest so the removal script prematurely pruned keys. That caused the JWKS to be single-key. I have a patch to restore retention and will add an integration test to ensure JWKS lists overlapping kids during rotations.
jenna_support: QA: ask customers who still see issues to capture `x-request-id` and timestamp. Also ask which SDKs — some older SDKs cache JWKS aggressively.
sarah_ops: noted multiple customers on old JS SDK 0.8.2 — their client cached JWKS indefinitely and needs forced refresh. We're adding a client-facing note to suggest restarting services / clearing cache as a short-term mitigation.
matt_reliability: telemetry: 08:10–08:25 window had ~22% auth failure rate. Post-rollout dropped to <1% by 08:30. We're still tracking edge cases.
luis_oncall: next steps for incident: - postmortem draft - add automated check in deploy pipeline that ensures `remove_legacy_key` isn't set without `force_window` and `staged_key_retention` present - run a canary that exercises JWKS rotation and token verification across versions - ops playbook update with explicit rollback steps and customer communication templates.
kai_auth: I've reverted the manifest, opened PR #6789 with tests, and will follow up with a rollback postmortem section. Also adding a flag `rotation.guardrails=true` to prevent manual omission.
jenna_support: customer comms: sending templated status updates now. I'll mark tickets as "Mitigated — follow-up required" and route to account teams for any lingering issues.
sarah_ops: final note — please attach any `auth-service` traces and `req ids` to the postmortem. I captured a sample trace for `req_8a7c9c`.
deploy-bot: runbook checkpoint: incident_state=mitigated, owner=luis_oncall, followup_prs=["#6789"], sla_breach=false.
matt_reliability: locking this thread for postmortem creation. Thanks everyone for quick response.
luis_oncall: I'll start the postmortem doc and ping on-call rotation for lessons. Action items assigned in the doc. Closing pager for now. :white_check_mark:
